Human cell markers, CD45 Monoclonal Antibody, Alexa FluorTM700, (2D1) (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and CD235a (Glycophorin A) Monoclonal Antibody, APC-eFluorTM780, (HIR2, GA-R2) (Thermo Fisher Scientific) were used at a final concentration of 0.03 μg/mL.
For bacterial staining, SYTOTM9 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) was used at a previously optimized final concentration of 5 μM (Mulroney et al., 2017).

Ammonium chloride (Sigma Aldrich, MO, United States), potassium bicarbonate (Sigma Aldrich) and EDTA (Sigma Aldrich) were added to 800 mL of MilliQ water for final concentrations of 0.15 M, 0.01 M, and 0.1 mM, respectively. The pH was adjusted to 7.2 and additional MilliQ water was added for a final volume of 1,000 mL. Aliquots were filtered (Millipore PVDF 0.2 μm syringe filter, Merck, Darmstadt, Germany) prior to use.

Whole blood from a heathy donor was stained with CD235a and further diluted in PBS (with 1% FBS, Moregate Biotech, QLD, Australia) in separate tubes. Yeast and human cell markers were added and further incubated for 30 min at the temperatures described previously. Samples were centrifuged at 400 × g for 5 min and washed in 1 mL PBS (with 1% FBS). An unstained sample was prepared in parallel. Samples were re-suspended in 1 mL of PBS and analyzed on the AttuneTM NxT (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

For the final method (Figure 2), spiked blood culture bottles were shaken and 5 mL of medium removed to a 15 mL centrifuge tube (Corning, New York). A 10 μL aliquot of sample was removed, plated on BA and incubated for 24–48 h to check for purity. Meanwhile, 5 mLs of 0.5% TritonTM X-100 solution (Sigma-Aldrich, SL, United States), prepared in sterile water were added to the tube, thoroughly vortexed and incubated at 35 °C for 10 min. Tubes were spun at 1,600 × g for 5 min and the supernatant discarded. The remaining pellet was re-suspended in 5 mL sterile water and incubated at 35 °C for 10 min to induce hypotonic lysis of human cells. Tubes were then spun again and the supernatant discarded. The pellet was re-suspended in 1 mL HBSS or PBS with serial dilutions performed in HBSS/PBS prior to staining and acquisition by flow cytometry with results available in just over 1 h. If visible aggregates of hyphae were evident in the re-suspension, samples were passed through a 70 μm cell strainer (Greiner Bio-One, Kremsmunster, Austria) prior to staining to prevent machine clogging.

Spiked bacterial blood culture bottles were processed, serially diluted into separate tubes and stained with SYTOTM9 as previously described prior to data acquisition. The same serial dilution without SYTOTM9, was then stained with CFW and ACF as described earlier. After staining, 250 μL of the suspension was transferred to a 96 well plate (Greiner Bio-One) in triplicate and run on the AttuneTM CytPixTM with the Autosampler (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Unstained samples were run first, followed by stained samples then “blank” wells with PBS to minimize event carry over between samples. The method was repeated for the negative control (un-spiked human blood) and the yeast positive controls (ATCC 10231 and ATCC 15545).

A clinical C. albicans isolate was spiked into 2 mL of donor blood for a standardized concentration of 3 × 106 cells/mL, mixed and cleaned-up as described previously. The processed sample was resuspended in 1 mL of PBS and diluted 1:10 in HBSS then stained with CFW and ACF. Data was acquired using the imaging flow cytometer. To determine the potential misclassification of cells, 600 events were randomly sampled from a total of 1,796 events captured in the YER by the CytpixTM (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Images of these events were visually inspected using Image J (v 1.54 p) and cells defined as yeast based on morphological characteristics including: size, shape, the presence of distinct cell walls and cells with a high refractivity (higher contrast to background).

To visualize the staining specificity of the yeast cell markers a clinical C. albicans isolate was spiked into a blood culture bottle, incubated for 48 h, then processed and stained as described earlier. After staining, the samples were diluted 1:10 in PBS and spun at 12, 000 × g for 5 min and the supernatant discarded. Cells were fixed in 4% formaldehyde (PierceTM 16% Formaldehyde (w/v), Methanol-free, ThermoFisher Scientific) for 20 min at room temperature, pelleted and then re-suspended in 50 uL PBS. Ten microliters of sample was added to Poly-L-Lysine coated slides (ProSciTech, Kirwan, QLD, Australia) and air dried in a biosafety cabinet. One drop of glycerol mounting medium was added (refractive index of 1.472), (ProSciTech) and covered with a coverslip (0.17 mm thickness) (ProSciTech). The sides were sealed with clear nail polish and air dried in the dark. Imaging was performed using the Nikon A1Si confocal microscope (Tokyo, Japan) (with a 20 × , 0.75-numerical-aperture dry lens, 3 × digital zoom) and the following lasers: 405 nm, 495 nm, and 640 nm. Sequential scanning was used, and images were collected using the NIS elements software (Version no: 5.02.03).

After fluorescent marker selection, the optimized method was applied to spiked blood cultures to determine the limit of detection (LOD) using flow cytometry and plate counts. Yeast isolates were grown on SAB as described earlier (n = 6, one isolate of each species) with single colonies emulsified into 10 mL YPD and grown for an additional 24–48 h at 35 °C. Overnight suspensions were enumerated using CFW as previously described and diluted to 3 × 106 cells/mL in PBS. Standardized inocula were prepared by serially diluting this suspension to a final concentration of 3 × 101 cells/mL in separate tubes. Multiple aliquots of 2 mL were sampled from a BC bottle supplemented with donor blood. One milliliter of standardized inocula or PBS (negative control) were added to the 2 mL aliquots. The blood culture clean-up process was performed immediately using TritonTM X-100 and water as previously described, with a final resuspension in 1 ml HBSS. For flow cytometric processing, samples were diluted 1:10 in HBSS and stained as described earlier. Unstained samples were run in parallel on the Attune NxT (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, United states) After staining, 250 μL of each sample was aliquoted into a 96 well plate (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, United States) in triplicate and data acquired using the AttuneTM NxT autosampler. For plate counts, serial dilutions of the re-suspended sample were prepared in PBS and 100 μL plated onto SAB plates in triplicate. Plates were incubated at 35 °C for 24–48 h and colonies counted.

Both flow cytometers were calibrated prior to each run according to the manufacturer's instructions (ThermoFisher Scientific) For yeast markers, flow cytometer settings were: Forward Scatter (FSC) voltage 100, FSC threshold 0.8 × 1,000 AND, Side Scatter (SSC) voltage 240, SSC threshold 0.7 × 1,000 AND, violet laser 1 (VL1 – 440/50 nm) (CFW) 185, blue laser 1 (BL1 – 530/30 nm) (ConA/Anti-Candida FITC) 310, and red laser 1 (RL1 – 670/14 nm) (EB) 300. The same settings were used for the human cell markers with the additional channels used: (CD45), 330, red laser 2 (RL2 - 720/30 nm) and (CD235a), 350, red laser 3 (RL3 – 780/60 nm). For bacterial spike experiments, the following settings were used to detect bacteria on scale: FSC voltage 340, FSC threshold 0.3 × 1,000 AND, SSC voltage 340, SSC threshold 0.2 × 1,000 AND, BL1 voltage 260 (SYTOTM9), BL1 threshold 0.1 × 1,000 AND, BL2 voltage 200.

steps.title: Culture and store yeast isolates
steps.instruction: Streak each clinical yeast isolate onto Sabouraud agar plates and incubate 48 h at 35 °C; for long‑term storage inoculate colonies into Yeast Extract‑Peptone‑Dextrose (YPD) broth with 20 % glycerol, aliquot into cryovials and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Culture and store bacterial isolates
steps.instruction: Streak each bacterial isolate onto blood agar plates (5 % sheep blood) and incubate 24 h at 35 °C; for long‑term storage emulsify colonies in Brain‑Heart‑Infusion broth with 20 % glycerol, aliquot and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 1 L ammonium chloride buffer
steps.instruction: Add ammonium chloride (final 0.15 M), potassium bicarbonate (final 0.01 M) and EDTA (final 0.1 mM) to 800 mL Milli‑Q water, adjust pH to 7.2, bring volume to 1 000 mL with Milli‑Q water, filter through a 0.2 µm PVDF syringe filter and aliquot for use.

steps.title: Prepare spiked blood culture bottles
steps.instruction: To each commercial BD Bactec™ Plus aerobic bottle add 10 mL donor whole blood (ethics‑approved) and later inoculate with a standardized yeast suspension to obtain a final concentration of 1 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare yeast inoculum for spiking
steps.instruction: Streak yeast isolates on SAB plates, incubate 48 h at 35 °C; emulsify single colonies in 1 mL sterile 1× PBS, enumerate by flow cytometry (Attune CytPix™) and adjust to ≈2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹; serially dilute in PBS, spike into blood‑culture bottles to reach 1 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹; confirm by plating 100 µL of 10‑fold dilutions on SAB plates (24–48 h at 35 °C).

steps.title: Prepare bacterial inoculum for spiking
steps.instruction: Streak bacterial isolates on blood agar, incubate 24 h at 35 °C; emulsify colonies in PBS, serially dilute, stain with SYTO™9 (5 µM) to enumerate, then spike into blood‑culture bottles as above (final 1 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹). Incubate spiked bottles 24 h at 35 °C before processing.

steps.title: Add human cell marker antibodies
steps.instruction: Add CD45‑Alexa Fluor™700 and CD235a‑APC‑eFluor™780 antibodies to each sample at a final concentration of 0.03 µg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Add SYTO9 for bacterial staining
steps.instruction: Add SYTO™9 to bacterial samples to a final concentration of 5 µM (as previously optimized).

steps.title: Lyse erythrocytes (whole‑blood samples)
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mL donor whole blood with 9 mL ammonium‑chloride buffer, incubate on ice 5 min, centrifuge 400 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, wash pellet with PBS + 1 % FBS, resuspend in 1 mL PBS, incubate 37 °C 15 min, dilute as required, then proceed to antibody staining on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Clean up spiked blood culture (Triton X‑100)
steps.instruction: Shake the spiked bottle, transfer 5 mL broth to a 15 mL centrifuge tube, remove a 10 µL aliquot and plate on blood agar (incubate 24–48 h) for purity check; add 5 mL of 0.5 % Triton™ X‑100 (in sterile water), vortex, incubate 35 °C 10 min, spin 1 600 × g 5 min, discard supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 5 mL sterile water, incubate 35 °C 10 min (hypotonic lysis of human cells).
Spin again 1 600 × g 5 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend final pellet in 1 mL HBSS or PBS.
If hyphal aggregates are visible, pass suspension through a 70 µm cell strainer before staining.

steps.title: Stain cleaned sample with yeast markers
steps.instruction: Add Calcofluor White (CFW) to a final concentration of 5 µg mL⁻¹ (with fixed Evan’s Blue ratio) and Anti‑Candida FITC (4–5 µg mL⁻¹, 1:1000 dilution) to the resuspended pellet; incubate 30 min at room temperature in the dark. For samples requiring ConA, add ConA‑CF®488A to 50 µg mL⁻¹ and incubate 30 min at 35 °C. Human‑marker‑stained tubes are kept on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Set flow cytometer parameters (yeast)
steps.instruction: Configure the Attune™ (or CytPix™) as follows: FSC voltage 100, FSC threshold 0.8 × 10³ AND; SSC voltage 240, SSC threshold 0.7 × 10³ AND; VL1 (440/50 nm, CFW) 185; BL1 (530/30 nm, ConA/Anti‑Candida FITC) 310; RL1 (670/14 nm, Evan’s Blue) 300. For human markers add RL1 (CD45) 330, RL2 (720/30 nm, CD235a) 350, RL3 (780/60 nm) as needed.

steps.title: Set flow cytometer parameters (bacteria)
steps.instruction: For SYTO9‑stained bacterial samples set: FSC voltage 340, FSC threshold 0.3 × 10³ AND; SSC voltage 340, SSC threshold 0.2 × 10³ AND; BL1 voltage 260 (SYTO9), BL1 threshold 0.1 × 10³ AND; BL2 voltage 200.

steps.title: Set acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Use a flow rate of 100 µL min⁻¹ for yeast samples (acquire 250 µL or stop after 10 000 events or 150 µL of sample); for bacterial spike experiments use 200 µL min⁻¹ and stop after 60 µL; for CytPix™ experiments stop after 100 µL. Run each sample in technical triplicate.

steps.title: Acquire data on flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Load 250 µL of each sample (unstained control, stained sample, PBS blank) into the autosampler 96‑well plate (triplicate wells); run unstained controls first, then stained samples, then blanks to minimize carry‑over.

steps.title: Analyze flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Export FCS files and import into FlowJo v10.10.0; concatenate technical triplicates, remove doublets using SSC‑H/SSC‑A, gate CD45⁺ and CD235a⁺ populations on histograms, apply these gates to yeast‑marker channels, exclude autofluorescence using unstained controls, then quantify yeast events in the Yeast Expected Region (YER).

steps.title: Perform parallel plate counts
steps.instruction: Serially dilute the final resuspended sample in PBS, plate 100 µL of each dilution onto SAB plates in triplicate, incubate 24–48 h at 35 °C and count colonies to obtain viable‑cell counts for validation.

steps.title: Prepare microscopy slide of C. albicans
steps.instruction: Spike a clinical C. albicans isolate into 2 mL donor blood (3 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹), clean‑up as above, stain with CFW and ACF, dilute 1:10 in PBS, centrifuge 12 000 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, fix pellet in 4 % formaldehyde for 20 min at room temperature, wash, resuspend in 50 µL PBS, place 10 µL on poly‑L‑lysine‑coated slide, air‑dry, add one drop glycerol mounting medium, cover with 0.17 mm coverslip, seal with nail polish, let dry in the dark, then image on Nikon A1Si confocal microscope (20×, 0.75 NA, 3× digital zoom) using 405 nm, 495 nm and 640 nm lasers; collect images with NIS‑Elements v5.02.03.

steps.title: Calculate limit of detection (LOD)
steps.instruction: For each LOD experiment, acquire yeast events as above, compute mean blank (cells in un‑spiked blood controls) and apply the Illingworth et al. (2018) equation after log₁₀‑transforming concentrations; calculate recovery efficiency from parallel plate‑count data (log₁₀‑transformed).
